Week in brief

Configuration Manager 2609 disables CMG storage shared-key access, clarifying reporting limits

All 3,607 recorded items were updates, and the supplied examples are overwhelmingly author-metadata maintenance rather than feature delivery. The meaningful administrator-facing changes cover CMG storage access and permissions for Configuration Manager 2609, co-management enrollment troubleshooting, Intune reporting scope for MDM Firewall and ASR policies, and revised Enterprise App Management blocking-app guidance. Configuration Manager TLS 1.2 instructions also received a terminology and procedure cleanup.

  • Configuration Manager · General
    CMG shared-key access is automatically disabled from Configuration Manager 2609

    The CMG security and privacy guidance now says shared-key access for CMG storage is automatically disabled beginning with Configuration Manager 2609, including existing deployments. It adds permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage, calls out Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor role assignments, and distinguishes storage keys from application secrets.

  • Configuration Manager · Device enrollment
    Co-management guidance adds a device-token enrollment prerequisite and fallback

    The Monitor Co-management guidance now specifies that device-token auto-enrollment requires Windows 10 version 1803 or later. If the device-token attempt fails, enrollment falls back to the user token; the page also directs administrators to ComanagementHandler.log when troubleshooting pending or failed enrollment.

  • Intune · Device security
    Security Settings Management documents policy-level MDM reporting

    For Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM, the updated guidance states that per-setting reporting is unavailable and only policy-level status is reported.

  • Enterprise App Management · App management
    Enterprise App Management removes its auto-update blocking-app restriction statement

    The revised page removes the statement that auto-update Enterprise App Catalog apps cannot be blocking apps in ESP or Autopilot device preparation. Administrators should use the current guidance when configuring those blocking-app scenarios.

  • Configuration Manager · General
    Configuration Manager TLS 1.2 server instructions clarify .NET and architecture handling

    The TLS 1.2 server page now uses consistent .NET terminology and provides clearer instructions for framework support, security updates, and registry subkey changes by application and operating-system architecture.

For Intune administrators

Most metadata-only edits require no action. For Configuration Manager 2609 CMG deployments, review the CMG server application and operator Azure RBAC permissions, especially permissions to create Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor role assignments. For co-management enrollment troubleshooting, verify Windows 10 version 1803 or later and inspect ComanagementHandler.log. Review MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules at policy level rather than per setting. Recheck current Enterprise App Management guidance before configuring auto-update Enterprise App Catalog apps as blocking apps in ESP or Autopilot device preparation.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.
